name: Alaska

law.summary: Wastewater operators must give DEC emergency notice of overflows and spills that threaten public health or water quality (18 AAC 72.940) and file 5-day noncompliance reports under APDES permits; no duty to tell the public was found.

citations.title: Emergency notice
citations.quote: an accident, spill, or other event that results in inadequate treatment in violation of permit conditions, or threatens public health or water quality ... a sludge carry-over, washout, or overflow
citations.who: owner or operator of a wastewater system

regulator_report.deadline: emergency notice (deadline not read); 5-day written noncompliance report (SOBE rows say '5-day reporting for noncompliance that may endanger health or the environment')

erule.notes: Alaska permittees file through EPA's NeT-SewerOverflow: Anchorage 43, Ketchikan 2, Denali NP 1. Median one day from start to receipt.

statewide_feed.latency: days (median 1 day to EPA receipt, then the daily ECHO extract)
statewide_feed.receiving_water: free text in a side table
statewide_feed.notes: Federal fallback only; no state list found (DEC spill database is bot-walled and covers oil and hazardous substances).

cso.notification_practice: No public notice found for Juneau's 3 CSO outfalls; the second CSO permit (Alyeska pipeline) is an inventory artefact.

sso.notes: Anchorage reports most; half are basement backups.

barriers.what: DEC spill database (DataDome) and Justia/LII copies of 18 AAC refused scripted reads
No public notice duty or operator web notices found

readiness.rationale: Only the federal SOBE extract: Anchorage's SSOs with points and times, a few days late. Juneau's CSOs get outfalls, the rain caution and the statement.

owner_questions: Show SOBE-only states with SOBE events as 'Dated reports, delayed' even though no state channel exists?
Ask Alaska DEC whether sewage spills are in the PPR spill database and whether an export is available.
surprise: Alaska's only overflow data is EPA's: Anchorage files every SSO electronically within about a day, while Juneau, the state's one CSO city, has no public channel at all.
